title: Generate a field-name list with an annotation processor

blocks.text: A compile-time processor extends `AbstractProcessor`, declares what it handles with `@SupportedAnnotationTypes`, and runs inside `javac`. It inspects elements through `javax.lang.model`, generates new files through the `Filer`, and reports problems through the `Messager`: a problem reported as an **ERROR fails the compilation**, with the message on the element.

`FieldNamesProcessor.FieldNames` (given, `SOURCE` retention) marks a class. Write `FieldNamesProcessor.process(...)`: for each class marked `@FieldNames`, generate a class `<Name>Fields` **in the marked class's own package** with
public static final java.util.List<String> NAMES = java.util.List.of(...);

listing the class's **instance** fields (not its `static` ones) in declaration order. `@FieldNames` on anything that is not a class is reported as an error on that element whose message contains `@FieldNames`.

rows: `@FieldNames class Point { int x; int y; String label; }`
`package demo.geo; @FieldNames class Place { static int COUNT; String name; double lat; }`
compilation fails with an error on `Shape`

blocks.text: The tests hand your processor to `javac` themselves, so no `META-INF/services` file is needed.

cases.says: Compiling @FieldNames class Point { int x; int y; String label; ... } generates PointFields whose NAMES is [x, y, label].
For demo.geo.Place the generated class is demo.geo.PlaceFields with NAMES [name, lat].
Counter's static COUNT and static final UNIT are left out: NAMES is [total, owner].
@FieldNames on interface Shape fails the compilation with an ERROR on Shape.java whose message contains @FieldNames.

concepts: A compile-time processor extends AbstractProcessor, names its annotations with @SupportedAnnotationTypes and its version with @SupportedSourceVersion, and generates files through the Filer.
A processor reports problems through the Messager, and an ERROR diagnostic fails the compilation.
